subject: Long-context evaluation recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Priya Suresh <priya.suresh@acmecorp.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Long-context eval call + next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we covered and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned: 

What we heard
- Primary goal: reliably summarize multi-section technical reports (20–30k tokens) without losing key action items or introducing hallucinations.
- Pain points: current model truncates at 8k tokens; summarization fidelity drops with long inputs; occasional safety/PII redactions needed.
- Success metric: 90% recall of named action items + <=5% factual regressions vs. human baseline on the 50-report eval set.

What Redwood recommended (high level)
- Run a long-context evaluation using two model families: 1) a 32k-window Llama-derivative (quantized) and 2) a transformer with segmented summarization (2-stage chunk+fusion) for throughput comparison.
- Evaluate truncation behavior on both: native 32k window vs. prefix chunking with overlap and fusion.
- Use our provided prompt set (attached v2) and the benchmark harness link for automated metrics.

Next steps
1) We will run an initial eval on a 50-report sample you approved. Deliverables: CSV with per-report recall/precision/regression flags, example outputs, and a short slide summary (5–7 slides).
2) Share recommended prompt templates and model configs for your infra team to validate locally if desired.
3) Schedule a follow-up POC sync week of Apr 12 to review results and decide on a PoC.

Attachments: prompt_set_v2.txt (prompt templates), acme_long_context_eval_results.csv (placeholder — will populate after run), redwood_recommendation_summary.pdf (short plan).

Benchmarks & docs:
- Internal benchmark: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/acme-long-context
- Eval harness (drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3Cacme-long-context

Open Qs from our side
- Are there any compliance constraints around sending de-identified report sections to Redwood-managed infra for initial eval? If yes, we can run the same harness on your Dedicated or Private deployment.

Thanks — looking forward to running this.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — useful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Truncation behavior: we saw the model drop the last section (conclusions + action items) on some runs. Can you confirm whether your 32k-window run preserves suffix content reliably or whether the behavior we saw is due to tokenization differences and how you handle sliding windows?

2) Summarization fidelity: how do you measure "regressions"? We need clear examples so our legal/comms folks can see the difference between omission vs. hallucinated facts.

3) Compliance: we cannot send PII even de-identified data to your hosted infra. We are open to a remote-run on our Dedicated instance or you providing a local harness we can run and share the CSV output.

Also attaching one of the reports that failed for context (redacted) — can you check the output and confirm which config would be least likely to drop the conclusions?

— Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Priya Suresh <priya.suresh@acmecorp.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Long-context eval call + next steps

Hi Alex — great questions, answered inline below. Also popped the initial eval artifacts into the shared drive link (see related links).

1) Truncation behavior- Short answer: native 32k-window models preserve suffix content if the full context is passed intact, but many practical issues can cause effective truncation: tokenization mismatches, pre-processing that strips metadata, or an inference pipeline that enforces a shorter max_input_length. For your failing report, the appendix was pushed past 8k after HTML-to-text conversion; with correct tokenization we keep the conclusions.

Recommendation: run the native 32k model variant we recommended (LlamaX-32k-q4f16) for a direct comparison. If you need deterministic suffix guarantees, our segmented chunk+overlap fusion (chunk size 6k tokens, 10% overlap, fusion prompt) is more robust for extremely long documents and reduces suffix loss at the cost of extra compute.

2) Measuring regressions- We flag two classes: omission (missing named action items or entities) and hallucination (asserted facts not present in source). The harness produces per-report tags plus diffs against the human baseline and a small set of qualitative notes. Example attached in the CSV for report_07 shows: 
  - omitted action: "Assign QA lead" (human) vs not present in model summary;
  - hallucinated date: model introduced "June 12" (no date in source).

3) Compliance options- Understood. Two options: a) we run the harness in your Dedicated/Private environment (we provide the Dockerized harness + instructions), or b) you run locally and upload the CSV only. For the initial pass, if you prefer to run locally, Connor can provide the harness and a short runbook.

Attachments added to drive: acme_long_context_eval_results.csv (initial placeholders replaced with preliminary metrics), prompt_set_v2.txt, redwood_recommendation_summary.pdf.

Suggested next step: Connor to share the harness + schedule a short runbook call (30m) to walk your infra team through the local run.

Thanks,
Marissa
